callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## Description

## Problem
`js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` has **CRAP 1512.8** (CC 51, 17.5% covered) — setup of the test-automation **rework** leg (`pr_test_automation_rework.json`). Almost untested; a failure here stalls rework of test PRs. Sibling in the same flow: `js/postTestReworkResults.js::action` **CRAP 1192** (CC 54, 26.9%) and `createPRIfMissing` **CRAP 272** (16 CC, 0% covered, same file); the file has 8 over-threshold functions (~1950 total).

## Goal
Both `action` functions < 100 CRAP; `createPRIfMissing` covered (CRAP <= 12).

## Suggested approach
1. Characterization tests for the setup (branch/PR resolution, input folder, config, working dir) and for post-results (commit & push verify, PR create-if-missing, status moves, comments).
2. Extract pure planners/parsers; keep side effects in a thin executor in unchanged order. (The ls-remote probes were just hardened in #913/#915 — keep `prHelper.remoteBranchExists/Sha` usage as is.)

## Acceptance
- Targets below the numbers above, no regression, test-automation rework tests green.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. ## Problem
`js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` has **CRAP 1512.8** (CC 51, 17.5% covered) — setup of the test-automation **rework** leg (`pr_test_automation_rework.json`). Almost untested; a failure here stalls rework of test PRs. Sibling in the same flow: `js/postTestReworkResults.js::action` **CRAP 1192** (CC 54, 26.9%) and `createPRIfMissing` **CRAP 272** (16 CC, 0% covered, same file); the file has 8 over-threshold functions (~1950 total).

## Goal
Both `action` functions < 100 CRAP; `createPRIfMissing` covered (CRAP <= 12).

## Suggested approach
1. Characterization tests for the setup (branch/PR resolution, input folder, config, working dir) and for post-results (commit & push verify, PR create-if-missing, status moves, comments).
2. Extract pure planners/parsers; keep side effects in a thin executor in unchanged order. (The ls-remote probes were just hardened in #913/#915 — keep `prHelper.remoteBranchExists/Sha` usage as is.)

- Targets below the numbers above, no regression, test-automation rework tests green.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.

Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Test name promises behaviour that is never asserted**

The test is named *"unexpected error → catch posts ❌ comment with fallback tracker and returns failure"*, but the body only asserts the result shape:

```javascript
assert.equal(result.success, false);
assert.contains(result.error, 'config unreadable');
```

Neither the ❌ tracker comment nor the fallback tracker is ever observed. The scaffolding reveals the intent that was abandoned mid-way: `fallbackTracker` and `createdWith` are declared, suppressed with `void fallbackTracker; void createdWith;`, and a standalone `trackers.js` load (`var trackers = loadModule(...)`) is asserted only for `trackers.createTracker` existing — it is never wired into the module under test, so it proves nothing about the catch-block fallback.

As the safety net for this refactor, a test whose name overstates its coverage is worse than none — future readers will trust a guarantee that isn't there. Either wire the fallback tracker into a fresh `loadPreCliTestReworkSetup` load (as the in-code comment says was the plan) and assert `postComment` carries the ❌ comment, or rename the test to match what it actually pins (result shape on config-load failure) and drop the dead scaffolding.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Pinned quirk is a real bug — file a follow-up ticket so it is not lost**

Pinning (rather than fixing) `refreshed.pr === undefined` is the right call under this ticket's "pure refactor, behaviour-preserving" contract, and the in-code comment plus the pinned test are commendably transparent. But let's be clear about what is being preserved: when `createPRIfMissing` creates a PR and the re-fetch succeeds, `findTestPRForTicket` returns the PR object itself — so `refreshed.pr` is `undefined`, `createPRIfMissing` returns `undefined`, and the auto-created PR **silently never receives the rework body update or summary comment**. That is operator-visible behaviour loss on a non-trivial path.

Two asks (both non-blocking for this PR):

1. File a follow-up gh ticket referencing this quirk (e.g. "test rework: auto-created PR never gets rework summary — `refreshed.pr` should be `refreshed`"), so the pinned test doesn't quietly enshrine the bug forever.
2. When it is fixed, the pinned test `refresh after creation finds the PR → downstream pr is refreshed.pr (undefined today — pinned quirk)` must be updated in the same PR — it will (correctly) fail.

💡 **SUGGESTION: Stray duplicated docblock opener**

Two consecutive `/**` lines open what becomes a single merged comment — syntactically valid but looks like a copy-paste slip:

```javascript
/**
/**
 * createPRIfMissing is internal (not exported) — its coverage is driven
 * ...
```

Drop the first `/**`.

💡 **SUGGESTION: Dead scaffolding in the `runPublishGates` direct test**

The test body starts with a harness (`var h = loadReworkActionHarness(...)` + `try { ... } catch (e) {}` + `void calls;`) whose only outputs — `err`, `calls`, and the `h` harness itself — are never used, then re-runs the same two scenarios properly via `h1`/`h2`. The first block is leftover from an earlier iteration; delete it (and the `var calls = [];`/`void calls;` pair) so the test reads as what it asserts.

💡 **SUGGESTION: Dead field in the harness return**

`loadReworkActionHarness` returns `cliMock: null` — no test consumes it (tests reach the CLI through `recorded.cli` and `deps.cliWrapper`). Drop the field to avoid implying the harness exposes the cli double.

## Problem
`js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` has **CRAP 1512.8** (CC 51, 17.5% covered) — setup of the test-automation **rework** leg (`pr_test_automation_rework.json`). Almost untested; a failure here stalls rework of test PRs. Sibling in the same flow: `js/postTestReworkResults.js::action` **CRAP 1192** (CC 54, 26.9%) and `createPRIfMissing` **CRAP 272** (16 CC, 0% covered, same file); the file has 8 over-threshold functions (~1950 total).

## Goal
Both `action` functions < 100 CRAP; `createPRIfMissing` covered (CRAP <= 12).

## Suggested approach
1. Characterization tests for the setup (branch/PR resolution, input folder, config, working dir) and for post-results (commit & push verify, PR create-if-missing, status moves, comments).

- Targets below the numbers above, no regression, test-automation rework tests green.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.

Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Pinned quirk is a real bug — file a follow-up ticket so it is not lost**

Pinning (rather than fixing) `refreshed.pr === undefined` is the right call under this ticket's "pure refactor, behaviour-preserving" contract, and the in-code comment plus the pinned test are commendably transparent. But let's be clear about what is being preserved: when `createPRIfMissing` creates a PR and the re-fetch succeeds, `findTestPRForTicket` returns the PR object itself — so `refreshed.pr` is `undefined`, `createPRIfMissing` returns `undefined`, and the auto-created PR **silently never receives the rework body update or summary comment**. That is operator-visible behaviour loss on a non-trivial path.

Two asks (both non-blocking for this PR):

1. File a follow-up gh ticket referencing this quirk (e.g. "test rework: auto-created PR never gets rework summary — `refreshed.pr` should be `refreshed`"), so the pinned test doesn't quietly enshrine the bug forever.
2. When it is fixed, the pinned test `refresh after creation finds the PR → downstream pr is refreshed.pr (undefined today — pinned quirk)` must be updated in the same PR — it will (correctly) fail.
